neighbours.label: A subject pronoun in present-tense running speech full of contractions, where the next token is likely 'm, 're or 's; the same pronouns in past-tense narration stay quiet
fire: "Look," said Tom. "You're the only one who knows; that's why I'm here. Right now I feel like you're my last hope."
When you're young and you're broke, it's tough. I know it's tough, and I think you're handling it well.
Don't worry about me. I'm fine, and we're nearly done. If it's late, I'll call and you'll know we're safe.
"Why me?" she asked. "Because you're smart, and I'm not. That's why we're talking, and it's why I'm paying."
I can't stay long. We're leaving soon because it's getting dark, and I'm sure you're busy too.
He's late again. I guess it's the traffic, but you're right that we're wasting time and I'm tired.
"Is that so?" said Mara. "Then you're wrong, and I'm glad. Now I think we're finished, and it's time."
If you're ready, we're going. I hope it's not far, because I'm hungry and you're slow.

notes: Card: ' I' x8, ' you' x7, ' it' x3, ' he' x3, ' we' x2, each followed by a contraction; logit effect of the + pole promotes ' are', ' am', ' is', so the - pole suppresses them. Probe: one-sentence items reach only 0.07-0.19, multi-sentence dialogue 0.42-0.59; past narration 0.12, title 'When They Eat' 0.15. Test items are multi-sentence for that reason.
